cacheLife - Default cache profiles
text_content:
Next.js provides a set of named cache profiles modeled on various timescales. If you don't specify a cache profile in the `` function alongside the `` directive, Next.js will automatically apply the “default” cache profile.
However, we recommend always adding a cache profile when using the `` directive to explicitly define caching behavior.
``undefined15 minutesINFINITE_CACHEDefault profile, suitable for content that doesn't need frequent updates``undefined1 second1 minuteFor rapidly changing content requiring near real-time updates``5 minutes1 minute1 hourFor content that updates frequently within an hour``5 minutes1 hour1 dayFor content that updates daily but can be slightly stale``5 minutes1 day1 weekFor content that updates weekly but can be a day old``5 minutes1 week1 monthFor content that updates monthly but can be a week old``5 minutes1 monthINFINITE_CACHEFor very stable content that rarely needs updating
The string values used to reference cache profiles don't carry inherent meaning; instead they serve as semantic labels. This allows you to better understand and manage your cached content within your codebase.

title: cacheLife - Custom cache profiles
text_content:
You can configure custom cache profiles by adding them to the [/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) option in your `` file.
Cache profiles are objects that contain the following properties:
````Duration the client should cache a value without checking the server.Optional````Frequency at which the cache should refresh on the server; stale values may be served while revalidating.Optional````Maximum duration for which a value can remain stale before switching to dynamic fetching; must be longer than ``.Optional - Must be longer than ``
The "stale" property differs from the [/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes) setting in that it specifically controls client-side router caching. While `` is a global setting that affects all instances of both dynamic and static data, the `` configuration allows you to define "stale" times on a per-function or per-route basis.
Good to know: The “stale” property does not set the `` header. It instead controls the client-side router cache.
